subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: Should OpenClaw core own a temp artifact provenance and cleanup model, and which parts should instead live in plugins, SDK seams, or ClawHub?
rationale: The safety goal fits current priorities, but implementation would touch storage policy, cleanup authority, agent/tool APIs, doctor/runtime guardrails, and core-vs-plugin boundaries that need maintainer intent before a safe repair can be queued.

options.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
options.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific audit/review classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.

options.title: Full core provenance registry
options.body: Build a core-owned temp artifact registry and cleanup policy for all first-class OpenClaw temp artifacts, accepting broader storage and janitor responsibility in core.

options.title: Decline broad core scope
options.body: Keep this out of core except for concrete bugs such as backup stale-temp cleanup, and steer workflow janitors to plugins or ClawHub packages.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails plus plugin seam
recommendation.body: Have core cover runtime-critical temp-path checks and a minimal SQLite-backed provenance seam, while workflow-specific audit/review classifications live in plugins or ClawHub packages.
